master.title: West's protraction of talks on security proposals may dramatically deteriorate Russia's position, Moscow won't allow this - Putin; Military scenario in Ukraine to have grave consequences, diplomatic solution needed - Scholz
master.content:
Duma vote on DPR/LPR recognition relied on public opinion - Putin

MOSCOW. Feb 15 (Interfax) - The Russian Duma vote on the recognition of the Donetsk (DPR) and Luhansk (LPR) People's Republics took public opinion into account, the region's problems should be resolved in accordance with the Minsk Agreements, Russian President Vladimir Putin said.

"The deputies in parliament, like those in any country, orient themselves toward public opinion, orient themselves toward their voters' opinion, and they subtly feel it," Putin told a press conference after talks with German Chancellor Olaf Scholz on Tuesday.

"It is completely obvious that in our country, a vast majority of people sympathize with Donbas residents, support them, and hope that the situation will change drastically for the better for them," Putin said.

"We must do everything for Donbas' problems to be solved, but do so, as the Federal Chancellor was saying, primarily in accordance with the not-yet-fully-realized potential of implementing the Minsk Agreements," he said.

Russia can't accept mere promises that Ukraine won't be NATO member - Putin

MOSCOW. Feb 15 (Interfax) - Russia wishes to resolve the problem of Ukraine's possible accession to NATO now, via a negotiating process, and it cannot be satisfied with the mere promise not to admit it to the alliance, Russian President Vladimir Putin said.

"You've just said a wonderful phrase: 'It's been said that Ukraine won't be in NATO within the next few years'. What does it mean 'it's been said'? You and we should understand what 'it's been said' means in relations between countries. We've been told for 30 years that NATO would not expand toward Russia's borders even for a day, but now we see NATO infrastructure right near our doorstep," Putin said in reply to a question from a reporter at a press conference following negotiations with German Chancellor Olaf Scholz on Tuesday.

Moreover, Ukraine's accession to NATO has been discussed, Putin said. "It's been said, as you put it, that this won't happen tomorrow. But when, then? The day after tomorrow? What does it change for us from the historical perspective? Absolutely nothing," he said.

"Russia hears that Ukraine is not prepared to join NATO today, and we know this premise. And they say right away that it won't be admitted tomorrow, but will be admitted when they prepare it for this. But this might be too late for us. Therefore, we want this issue to be settled now, right now, in the near future, through a negotiating process, by peaceful means," Putin said.

Russia assumes this position and really hopes that its partners will listen to its concerns and take them seriously, Putin said.

West's protraction of talks on security proposals may dramatically deteriorate Russia's position, Moscow won't allow this - Putin

MOSCOW. Feb 15 (Interfax) - Moscow will not allow unfounded protraction of talks on security guarantees, because during this time the West may take steps that will exacerbate Russia's position, Russian President Vladimir Putin said.

"We are concerned that the negotiations on security issues essential for us that we have proposed may be groundlessly protracted by our partners, and during these negotiations decisions will be made that will deteriorate our position in a very serious way, just as has been the case for many years," he said at a press conference following talks with German Chancellor Olaf Scholz.

"This is what is in our sight, what we understand, what we will discuss with our partners and what we will not allow," Putin added.

U.S., NATO responses to Russia's proposals on security guarantees contain several considerations that Moscow willing to discuss - Putin

MOSCOW. Feb 15 (Interfax) - Russian President Vladimir Putin has said that the U.S. and NATO responses to Russia's proposals on security guarantees have a number of considerations that Moscow has offered in previous years and stands ready to discuss now.

"I reiterate that the responses we received from the United States and other NATO countries to our proposals on security guarantees, in our opinion, do not meet the three basic Russian requirements. However, the responses we have received, nevertheless, include, as the Russian foreign minister reported to me yesterday, a number of considerations which we not only do not mind discussing, but, in fact, we proposed them to our partners in previous years - on European security, on certain weapon systems, we mean shorter- and intermediate-range missiles, and military transparency," Putin said at a press conference following talks with German Chancellor Olaf Scholz in Moscow on Tuesday.

"We stand ready to continue this joint work. We are also willing to proceed along the negotiating track, but all issues, as it was stated earlier, should be considered in their entirety, without separating them from the main Russian proposals, the implementation of which is an unconditional priority," the Russian president said.

Putin believes Scholz determined to develop pragmatic cooperation between Germany, Russia

MOSCOW. Feb 15 (Interfax) - Russian President Vladimir Putin said that his negotiations with German Federal Chancellor Olaf Scholz have passed in a businesslike atmosphere.

"During today's negotiations, which passed in a businesslike atmosphere, we substantively and extensively discussed a number of aspects of our bilateral relations and prospects of their development," Putin said at a press conference following the talks on Tuesday.

"Certainly, we attached special significance to the most relevant problems on the international agenda," he said.

"We've always sought to strengthen interaction between our states," Putin said.

"There's an impression that the federal chancellor is also predisposed toward pragmatic and mutually beneficial cooperation," he said.

Russia to act on Ukrainian border in accordance with real situation - Putin

MOSCOW. Feb 15 (Interfax) - Russian President Vladimir Putin, when asked whether Russia will continue withdrawing troops from the Ukrainian border, has said that the country will act according to a plan that depends on the real situation.

"How will Russia continue to act? By the plan. And what will it consist of? The real situation on the ground," Putin said at a press conference following talks with German Chancellor Olaf Scholz.

"Who can answer how the situation will unfold? No one can yet. It doesn't depend on us alone," Putin said.

At the same time, the Russian president noted that Russia "will strive to reach agreements with our partners on the issues that we have raised in order to resolve them diplomatically."

"What are these issues? This is well known in relation to ensuring Russia's security. These are NATO non-enlargement, the transfer of the bloc's military infrastructure to [the positions of] 1997 and the non-deployment of offensive arms near our borders," Putin said.

"Everything, in my opinion, is understandable and clear. We are willing to talk about other issues that are contained in the reply we received [from the United States and NATO], but in combination with what is of paramount value and paramount importance for us," the Russian president said.

Military scenario in Ukraine to have grave consequences, diplomatic solution needed - Scholz

MOSCOW. Feb 15 (Interfax) - German Chancellor Olaf Scholz has warned of severe economic and political consequences in the event that Russia takes military action against Ukraine.

"It's quite clear to the federal government that any further military aggression against Ukraine will lead to severe political, economic and strategic consequences. It seemed to me that everybody knew that," Scholz said at a press conference that he attended together with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday.

Scholz highlighted, however, that such escalation must be avoided at all costs. "The search for diplomatic solutions is one of the key reasons why I visited Kyiv yesterday and am visiting Moscow today," he said.

TCG to discuss Donbas status bill - Scholz

MOSCOW. Feb 15 (Interfax) - The Trilateral Contact Group (TCG) on Donbas will discuss draft legislation regarding a special status for the region, a constitutional reform in Ukraine, and the Steinmeier formula, German Chancellor Olaf Scholz said.

"It is so important that everyone make their contribution. One is to submit legislation necessary for discussing how to resolve the three big problems I have mentioned, relating to the special status, the elections, the Steinmeier formula, and of course constitutional issues. All this will be presented in the trilateral format, between Russia, Ukraine and the OSCE, and discussed with other parties involved. That's what we agreed," Scholz told a press conference after talks with the president of Russia in Moscow on Tuesday.

Everyone should support and not delay this process, he said.

Scholz sees Navalny's conviction as inconsistent with legal standards of rule-of-law state

MOSCOW. Feb 15 (Interfax) - German Chancellor Olaf Scholz said he views the conviction of Russian opposition activist Alexei Navalny as inconsistent with the legal standards of a rule-of-law state.

"As concerns Navalny, my position here is absolutely clear: his conviction is inconsistent with a rule-of-law state's standards. I've stressed this several times," Scholz said following negotiations with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday, when asked to comment on the start of Navalny's new trial.

Moscow's Lefortovsky District Court on Tuesday started hearing a new criminal case against Navalny at judicial proceedings arranged at the penitentiary in the Vladimir region where Navalny is currently serving his term.

Scholz voices concern about Memorial society

MOSCOW. Feb 15 (Interfax) - German Chancellor Olaf Scholz has said he is concerned about the narrowing space for civil society in Russia, particularly the prohibition of the Memorial society, which is designated as a foreign agent NGO in Russia and whose liquidation has been ordered by a court.

"The space for civil society is becoming narrower and narrower. Such partners with whom we've worked for a long time, for instance, Memorial [...] Germany cannot understand why the Memorial group should stop its activity," Scholz said at a press conference following negotiations with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Tuesday.

Memorial "has made an important contribution to clarifying the fates of Soviet citizens who were taken to Germany for forced labor [during WWII]," Scholz said.

"I hope good prospects are possible here," he said.
